site: Millevaches massif (Limousin, western French Massif Central) vs Bourbon l'Archambault foreland basin
region: European Variscides (French Massif Central internal zone)
method: hydrogen isotope paleoaltimetry (dD of meteoric water) + modern dD lapse rate (~-22 permil/km)
material_or_proxy: dD of synkinematic muscovite in detachment shear zone vs freshwater shark remains in foreland basin
notes: Abstract: dD water -96+/-8 permil (Millevaches) vs -20+/-6 permil (Bourbon l'Archambault), ~76 permil difference, consistent with 3.4+/-0.7 km. The companion Goldschmidt 2021 abstract calls this a minimum estimate, so hi_m is left open. Fluid-rock interaction ~318-310 Ma (40Ar/39Ar); the foreland reference is ~295 Ma, so the pair is not strictly coeval. Uses dD of meteoric fluid recorded in muscovite, not igneous whole-rock chemistry. Coordinates approximate (Millevaches/Felletin area).

site: Quiberon and Piriac detachment shear zones, Armorican Massif, Brittany
method: hydrogen isotope paleoaltimetry (dD of meteoric water) relative to foreland basin
material_or_proxy: dD of synkinematic muscovite in detachment shear zones
reference_short: Dusseaux C. 2019 PhD thesis Univ. Plymouth
notes: Thesis abstract: minimum elevation difference 2500+/-900 m between Armorican Massif internal zones and the Bourbon l'Archambault basin taken as near sea level; also 3300+/-1000 m for the Massif Central (not repeated here; superseded by the 2021 EPSL row). Age bracket from 40Ar/39Ar muscovite ~319-303 Ma for Quiberon (Dusseaux et al. 2022 J Struct Geol, 10.1016/j.jsg.2022.104546). The published Terra Nova paper (Dusseaux et al. 2019, 10.1111/ter.12392) gives meteoric dD as low as -74 permil but no elevation in its abstract. Weak: unpublished thesis value. Minimum, so hi_m open. DOI is DataCite (verified there, not CrossRef).

method: geodynamic model (critical wedge + flexural loading constrained by foreland basin thickness)
notes: Abstract: Early Permian central Appalachians had a central-Andean topography with average relief 3.5-4.5 km and width 250-300 km. Model-based and expressed as relief, not elevation above sea level. Age bracket is the Cisuralian (Early Permian, ICS). elev_m is midpoint (ours). Weak: tectonic model, not a paleoaltimeter.

site: Ames Limestone (Glenshaw Fm, Conemaugh Gp), Appalachian foreland basin, Ohio-West Virginia-Pennsylvania
material_or_proxy: marine limestone with benthic paleocommunities (Late Pennsylvanian cyclothem)
notes: Marine paleocommunities of the Upper Pennsylvanian Ames Limestone, the most widespread Late Pennsylvanian marine incursion into the Appalachian foreland. Age bracket is the Late Pennsylvanian (Kasimovian-Gzhelian, ICS) from the title. Abstract not accessed. Coordinates approximate (outcrop belt centroid).

site: Sierra del Cuera carbonate platform, Cantabrian Zone, Asturias
material_or_proxy: high-relief, steep-margined shallow-water carbonate platform and slope
reference_short: Bahamonde J.R. et al. 2004 Sed Geol
notes: Platform top records sea level in the Variscan foreland of the Ibero-Armorican arc during Bashkirian-Moscovian time; age bracket is the Bashkirian-Moscovian stage span (ICS) from the title. Slope facies lie below sea level. Abstract not accessed. Coordinates approximate.

site: Auernig Group cyclothems, Carnic Alps, Austria-Italy
region: Southern margin of the Variscides (sea-level datum)
notes: Title: cool-water carbonates in a paleoequatorial shallow-water environment, Upper Pennsylvanian Auernig cyclic sediments. Age bracket is the Late Pennsylvanian (ICS). Abstract not accessed. Coordinates approximate (Nassfeld area).

site: Permian Basin (Midland and Delaware basins), foreland of the Marathon orogen, West Texas
material_or_proxy: marine basin fill of the Marathon foreland
reference_short: Yang K.-M. & Dorobek S.L. 1995 SEPM Spec Publ 52
notes: Abstract: the Permian Basin lies in the foreland of the Marathon-Ouachita belt; the paper presents flexural models with the Marathon belt as the dominant topographic load. The abstract does not state facies or ages; the marine Early Permian fill is assumed from regional knowledge and the age bracket is the Cisuralian (ICS). Any Marathon load height from the flexural model was not accessed. Weak because facies and ages were not read from the source.
